text:
Emma Li: Hey team, escalating an odd SCIM provisioning case reported by ACME. New hires are created in our console but they're showing up with no roles (Org Member instead of Admin/Editor) and can't access dedicated projects. Customer says this started after they reconfigured their Okta app last night.

Jason (ACME): Yup. Just onboarded 6 people via SCIM import this morning. All users provisioned but none of them got the expected roles. We map Okta groups to Redwood roles (okta group -> redwood role). Worked until yesterday.

Emma Li: Thanks Jason. Can you paste a sample SCIM payload you see in Okta (Provisioning > View Logs > Request)? A PATCH or POST body would help.

Jason (ACME): Here you go (sanitized):
```
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
  "userName": "j.smith@acme.com",
  "name": {"givenName": "John","familyName": "Smith"},
  "emails": [{"value": "j.smith@acme.com"}],
  "groups": [{"display": "Platform-Admin"},{"display":"eng-team"}]
}
```

Priya Narayan (Identity Eng): Quick question: do they send group display names or group IDs? Our mapping layer expects group names case-sensitive (exact match) by default.

Jason (ACME): Okta sends display attribute. I verified group display names are Platform-Admin and Eng-Team (capital E/T). But in the payload it was eng-team (lowercase) for some users — looks like Okta normalization may have been toggled.

Emma Li: Sounds like a group name case mismatch. But also note we recently rolled a change to accept both displayName and value as inputs (last week). Could be a regression. @priya can you check the mapping logs for org acme when user j.smith was created? Request id: req_0a9c3f2 (from customer logs).

Priya Narayan: Looking now. I see the provisioning request hit our /scim/v2/Users endpoint at 2026-03-01T09:12:14Z. We logged the group parsing step and it shows groups: ["Platform-Admin","eng-team"]. Our role mapper consulted the group->role table and only matched "Platform-Admin" to role:admin. "eng-team" wasn't found due to case mismatch (our keys are "Eng-Team").

Marco Tanner (Eng Infra): Did the customer have any renaming rules in Okta (e.g., transform to lowercase)? Okta has a setting to "lowercase group names" in SCIM integration at the app level.

Jason (ACME): We did flip a normalization option last night when tidying group names; didn't think it would matter.

Emma Li: That explains missing admin role for some users. But customer also reported one user didn't get deprovisioned when removed from Okta yesterday — any logs on DELETE/DEPROVISION flow?

Priya Narayan: There's a related PATCH event at 2026-03-01T10:05:02Z that removed group membership on our side but the account stayed active because our webhook to the tenant service failed with 502. The scim-bot retried twice but hit the same gateway error. We have a record: scim_event_20260301_100502 -> webhook_status:502.

scim-bot: Automated note: retry scheduled in 30s (attempt 2/3) for event scim_event_20260301_100502.

Marco Tanner: 502 went to tenant-api behind alb. I pulled logs — there was a transient surge and a circuit breaker; the webhook ultimately timed out. We should've marked the event as 'pending' and retried longer. I'll open a patch.

Emma Li: For now can we give ACME a mitigation: run a manual sync job or re-run provisioning for those users? Jason, can you re-provision the affected user(s) while we patch?

Jason (ACME): Will try re-provision for the 6 users. Do you want me to trigger a full push or just edit group membership in Okta to match case?

Priya Narayan: Two-pronged: 1) Fix customer side to preserve group case (recommended). 2) We'll make our role-mapper case-insensitive and add a canonicalization step to tolerate common normalization (lower/upper/kebab/camel). I'll schedule a hotfix for role mapping and add telemetry to flag unmapped groups.

Emma Li: Can you estimate timeline for hotfix? Customer is in paid Dedicated contract and needs stable access.

Priya Narayan: I can push a scoped change to the role-mapper within 2 hours (config change + unit tests) and deploy to staging. If staging looks good, deploy to prod in next maintenance window (or we can do an emergency deploy with a short rollback plan).

Marco Tanner: Also I'll add retry/backoff improvements to the webhook handler for SCIM deprovision events. That will address the 502 deprovision misses. That patch will need a deploy and smoke test — estimate 6 hours.

Emma Li: Good. Jason — I'll coordinate with you on a manual sync. Meanwhile Priya, once hotfix is up, can we backfill roles for ACME automatically? We can run a reconciliation that scans users with 'Org Member' default and maps groups -> roles with the new canonical logic.

Priya Narayan: Yes, we can run one-off reconciliation for ACME after deploy. I will prepare a dry-run report first and share with Emma.

Jason (ACME): Thanks. I'm going to re-run the push now (Okta -> SCIM). I'll post results.

Jason (ACME) [10:20]: Re-provision completed. 6 users now show roles for 2 of them but 4 still Org Member.

Emma Li: Can you send one of the userIds that still didn't get role? We'll run reconciliation after hotfix.

Jason (ACME): user ids: u_123, u_124, u_125, u_126.

Priya Narayan: Confirmed. Those users arrived with groups lowercased in payload. Our current prod mapping didn't match. Hotfix branch created: feature/role-mapper-case-insensitive. Running unit tests now.

Priya Narayan [11:05]: Hotfix deployed to staging. No regressions on mapping tests. Running ACME dry-run using their sample payloads via staging endpoint — mapping shows roles applied correctly.

Emma Li: Marco, any concerns pushing role-mapper change to prod now? It should be low-risk but affects all orgs.

Marco Tanner: It's config + matching logic only, no schema changes. We'll do canary deploy to 5% of orgs for 30 minutes, monitor trace for unmapped groups and error rates, then roll to 100% if healthy. I'll schedule canary in 1 hour.

scim-bot: Deploy event: feature/role-mapper-case-insensitive -> canary 5% at 12:30 UTC.

Priya Narayan: I'm also enabling telemetry: unmapped_group_count, normalized_group_key. We'll watch ACME org specifically.

Emma Li: Post-deploy action: once canary shows ACME mapping fixed, run reconciliation for those 4 users. Marco, do you want to coordinate the webhook retry fix in a separate ticket?

Marco Tanner: Yep. Created ENG-3427 SCIM webhook retry/backoff. Will start immediately after canary verification.

Priya Narayan [13:05]: Canary healthy at 5%, no errors. Rolling to 100% now.

scim-bot: Deploy event: rollout -> 100% completed at 13:12 UTC.

Priya Narayan: Role mapping hotfix live. Running automated reconciliation for org acme now (dry-run succeeded). I'll send the reconciliation patch and then flip to write mode to update roles for u_123,u_124,u_125,u_126.

Priya Narayan [13:20]: Reconciliation applied. Users updated to Admin/Editor as expected.

Jason (ACME): Confirmed — all 6 users now have correct roles and can access the projects. Thank you!

Emma Li: Closing loop: root causes were 1) Okta normalization toggled to lowercase group names and 2) a transient webhook failure prevented deprovisioning earlier. Fixes: a) role-mapper made canonical/case-insensitive + telemetry; b) ENG-3427 to improve webhook retries. Also recommended customer action: disable group name lowercasing or ensure group display names match mapping.

Jason (ACME): We'll disable the lowercase transform and monitor. Appreciate the quick turnaround 🎉.

Emma Li: I'll mark as resolved and create a postmortem summary to share with ACME and internal docs (incidents/ and knowledge base). Thanks @priya @marco for quick triage. :shipit:
